final_message:
I built the Ploverdesk landing page, but I could not build or open it here: the sandbox won't run Node, so `npm run build` never ran. I checked the types by reading the code, which is not the same as compiling it.

**What I built**
- **First screen:** the headline and the trial button, next to an example supplier invoice matched line by line against its purchase order and delivery note. It's labelled "Illustrative values, not customer data". Three of its six lines are flagged in red with the reason in words (unit price differs, invoiced more than was delivered, never delivered). The matched lines are grey. A "Hide matched lines" button fades the matched lines out in 160ms and leaves only the flagged ones. That fade is the page's only animation, and it is instant when the visitor has reduced motion turned on.
- **Further down:** how an invoice moves through Ploverdesk (arrives by email, matched, exceptions to a person, the rest to payment approval and the accounting system); a short terms list (290 EUR a month per company, no user limit, 14-day trial without a card, CSV or API export, hosted in Frankfurt); and a "Who builds it" paragraph (six people in Rotterdam, founded 2025). That paragraph says plainly there are no customer logos or quotes yet. "Start the 14-day trial" (/trial) is the one main action, and "Book a demo" (/demo) is always a plain link.
- **Look:** cool white background, near-black text, a dark petrol blue used only for buttons and links, a single red used only for values that don't match. System fonts, figures that line up in columns, sharp corners, thin lines, no shadows, nothing moving on scroll.
- **Narrow screens:** below about 640px each invoice line becomes a small block with every value under its label.

**Decisions I made on my own, since nobody could answer**
- The visual and interaction direction is my own proposal and nobody approved it. It is written out at the top of `MASTER.md`.
- **The example invoice's quantities and prices are made up.** The brief says to invent no figure. I read that as covering claims about the company (customers, results), and labelled these as illustrative on the page. If the founders read it more strictly, the example table has to go.
- I made the example invoice come from a food supplier. Nothing in the brief says which goods; it's easy to change.
- No web font: there's no network, and adding a Google Fonts request needs someone's agreement.

**Checks I ran**
- **Static audit:** 28 checks, two flagged, and I judged neither a real problem:
  - Hover with no transition: the transitions are set on the base rules (`src/index.css:82,101,124`).
  - Animation driven by a timer: the timer only removes the rows once the CSS fade has finished, using the duration token (`src/ExampleMatch.tsx:66`). It doesn't drive the animation frame by frame.
- **Contrast:** computed from the colour values. All text passes: 17.5:1 for main text, 4.8:1 for the grey matched lines, 5.5:1 for red on its tint, 9.2:1 for white on the button. The toggle's border is right at the minimum, 3.0:1.
- **Three patterns still need a person's yes:** thin lines on each table row, the example invoice values, and the founding year. I listed them as intended in the direction, but since nobody approved it, they count as open.

**What I could not verify**
- `npm run build` (`tsc --noEmit && vite build`).
- The page in a browser at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px. At 1280×720, the status line under the example may fall just below the fold.
- A performance recording of the toggle in Chrome DevTools (no dropped frames).
- The page with the operating system's reduce-motion setting on.

`bunshin` (genjutsu's multi-agent pipeline for whole sites) didn't fit a single page, so I didn't use it.

Files are in `src/`:
- `App.tsx`
- `ExampleMatch.tsx`
- `tokens.css`
- `index.css`

Also changed:
- `index.html` (title and description)
- `MASTER.md` (the design system)
- `preview/thesis.html`
- `preview/design-system.html`

